items.title: CleanYourTV for LG webOS
items.text: A fast home screen for rooted LG webOS TVs. It replaces LG's Home with a dock of four apps, a top shelf and an app grid, and adds Live TV from your own playlist, an Inputs list on the Input key, picture notifications from your network, optional on-device voice recognition, and an optional debloat of LG's ads and telemetry.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
• Launcher. A dock of four apps, a top shelf with the focused app's name and an ambient glow, an app grid sorted by how often you use each app, an Inputs picker, a Settings shortcut and a clock. More.
  • Live TV. Plays your M3U playlist with a channel list, a programme guide (XMLTV) and number entry. It does not use LG's tuner. More.
  • Input key. The remote's Input button opens an Inputs list over the running app. More.
  • Picture notifications. A card with a photo over whatever is on screen, triggered from your network, for example by Home Assistant. More.
  • Voice (optional). Speech recognition on the TV (Moonshine), with answers from Home Assistant's Assist, a language model through OpenRouter or your own server, shown as text. More.
  • Debloat. Stops LG's ad and telemetry services and blocks a few ad servers. More.
  • Manager app. Sets up, updates and removes everything from the TV. More.

LG's system files are not modified. The launcher takes over Home with a mount that exists only in RAM, so a reboot without the boot scripts brings LG's Home back. Everything we install is stored in /media/developer/cleanyourtv (plus two boot scripts and the key binds), and the uninstall removes it. The project has no server or account and collects no data; optional features contact the services you choose (update checks go to GitHub). See What it changes on the TV and Security.

items.title: Compatibility at a glance
items.text:
Needs An LG webOS TV that is rooted with the Homebrew Channel, and SSH access as root for the install command. webOS webOS 5 and newer (2020 models and later). webOS 4 and older have no systemd and an old Node.js; setup stops before it changes anything. Tested LG OLED65G26LA on webOS 25. Other TVs are reported in Tested TVs. Not needed A computer app, a server, a cloud account. The service runs on the TV.

This modifies a TV with root access

Read install.sh and the scripts it installs before you run them, and use the project at your own risk. The setup saves the original state, and a failed start restarts the TV with LG's Home, but nothing here is covered by a warranty.

items.title: Where to start
items.text:
1. Make sure the TV is rooted and has the Homebrew Channel (rootmy.tv).
  2. Follow Installing: one command from your computer, then Set up now in the app on the TV.
  3. Check the tested TVs and report yours if it is not listed.

items.text: CleanYourTV is an independent project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by LG Electronics. LG and webOS are trademarks of LG Electronics. Live TV plays only the playlists you add; the project provides no channels and no playlist.

items.title: Working on problems with an AI assistant
items.text: If something does not work on your TV, an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, a local model) can help you find out why, and, if you want, help you fix the bug in the code and send the fix. This page says what to give it and how to keep it safe. Nothing here is required: Share log and an issue work as before.

items.title: The ground rules
items.text:
• Read-only first. The assistant reads a report. It may run read-only commands on the TV. Anything that changes the TV (restart a service, edit a file, install, delete, reboot) is proposed first, you say yes, and it names the command that undoes it.
  • You decide what leaves your house. A report goes to whatever AI service you use. Addresses, MAC addresses, stream URLs and tokens are masked, but masking is best effort: read the file before you paste or upload it. A local model keeps it on your computer.
  • An assistant can be wrong. Do not run a command you do not understand. The way back is always the same: switch CleanYourTV as Home off in the manager app, or sh /media/developer/cleanyourtv/undo-home.sh, or start the TV in the Homebrew Channel's failsafe mode.

items.title: Part 1: find out what is wrong on your TV
items.text:
1. Collect a report. In the manager app Share log shows a QR code for a masked report, or from your computer:
git clone https://github.com/lasharor/cleanyourtv-WebOS && cd cleanyourtv-WebOS
sh tools/diagnose.sh <tv-ip> > cytv-diagnose.txt

diagnose.sh logs in as root over SSH (key authentication, as set up by the Homebrew Channel) and only reads: the Share log report, the foreground and running apps, the media pipelines, the processes, the Input key mode, the configuration with secrets hidden, the themes on the TV, the service's last operations and the Live TV status. It changes nothing. Open the file and remove anything private. 2. Give the assistant the context. Start the conversation with AGENTS.md (what the project is, where the TV keeps things, what has gone wrong before, the rules) and the report. Tools that read the repository (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar) pick AGENTS.md up by themselves when you open the folder you cloned. 3. Ask for a diagnosis, not a fix. See the prompts below. Ask it to name the evidence in the report for each conclusion. 4. Try what it suggests, one step at a time, and tell it what happened. If it is a real bug, open an issue with the report and the assistant's findings, or go on with Part 2.

items.title: Prompts
items.text:
Diagnose a report

I use CleanYourTV on an LG webOS TV. Read AGENTS.md first. Below is a diagnostic report (tools/diagnose.sh) and this is what is wrong: describe it: what you did, what you expected, what happened, how often. Work out the most likely causes from the report. For each, quote the lines of the report that support it, and say what would show that it is wrong. Propose read-only checks first. Do not suggest a change to the TV without the exact command, what it does and the command that undoes it. Do not ask me for secrets.

Check the TV live (an agent with SSH)

You may run read-only commands on my TV with ssh root@<tv-ip> (cat, ls, ps, curl to 127.0.0.1:8765, luna-send queries with </dev/null). Do not change, restart, install, delete or reboot anything without asking me first, and name the undo command. Start from AGENTS.md and tools/diagnose.sh. The problem: describe it. Tell me what you found and what you would try next.

Understand the code behind a symptom

Using AGENTS.md ("Where things are") find the code responsible for symptom in this repository. Explain how it works on webOS ⅚ (Node 8.12) and on webOS 25, and list what could make it fail on a TV that is not the maintainer's.

items.title: Part 2: fix the bug and send the fix
items.text:
You need a copy of the repository on your computer, Node.js 22 or newer, and an assistant that can edit files and run commands (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot agent mode and similar). The project's rules are in AGENTS.md; the assistant reads them.

  1. Fork and clone, and make a branch: git checkout -b fix-short-description.
  2. Reproduce the bug. From the report, then from the code. Many bugs can be reproduced without a TV: the service runs under sh tools/node8-check.sh (Node 8.12.0, as on webOS 5 and 6), and the launcher page runs in Chrome against a stand-in service (see tools/theme-preview.mjs for the idea).
  3. Write a test that fails, then fix the code until it passes. A test in tools/node8-check.js is expected whenever the bug can be tested without a TV. Keep to the compatibility rules (Node 8.12 for the service, ES5 style for the pages).
  4. Run everything: sh tools/node8-check.sh, and python3 ipk/build.py to check that the package builds.
  5. Try it on a TV if you can: push the branch and every push publishes a test build (a pre-release named test-<branch>); in the manager app Update channel installs it, and Update channel > Stable releases goes back. Say in the pull request what you checked on a TV and what you did not.
  6. Open a pull request with the template. Describe the cause, not only the change, and say that AI tools were used.

What a pull request needs: the tests pass under Node 8.12, a new test for the bug where possible, the documentation page changed when the behaviour changed, no private data (addresses, tokens, playlist URLs, names), an honest note on what was verified on a real TV, and a line saying which AI tools helped. It is reviewed like any other pull request.

items.title: Prompts
items.text:
Fix a bug

Read AGENTS.md. Issue: paste the issue text and the masked report. Reproduce the problem (a failing test in tools/node8-check.js if it can be tested without a TV), find the cause, and make the smallest fix that follows the rules in AGENTS.md (Node 8.12 for the service, ES5 style for the pages, no private data). Run sh tools/node8-check.sh and python3 ipk/build.py. Update the documentation if behaviour changes. Do not commit to main, do not release. Tell me what is verified and what only a real TV can verify.

Review a change

Review my change against AGENTS.md: Node 8.12 compatibility, ES5 style in the pages, private data, missing tests, documentation that no longer matches, and anything that could leave a TV in a state it cannot recover from (boot scripts, mounts, the update path).

Write the pull request text

From the diff, write a pull request description: the symptom, the cause, what changed, how it was tested (name the commands), what was checked on a real TV and what was not, and a line that AI tools were used.

items.title: What the assistant should not do
items.text:
• Run commands on your TV that change it, without asking you first.
  • Paste your tokens, playlist address, IP addresses or names into an issue or a pull request.
  • Release, tag or force-push. The maintainer releases.
  • Copy code from GPL projects into this MIT project.

items.title: Notes for maintainers
items.text: AGENTS.md (and CLAUDE.md, which points to it) is the briefing; keep it short and correct when the layout, the TV facts or the rules change. The issue form asks for the Share log and, if used, the assistant's findings; the pull request template asks for the checks above.

items.title: Service API
items.text:
The service runs as root on 127.0.0.1:8765 and answers JSON. It is what the launcher, the manager and the other apps use, and you can call it from a shell on the TV (for example over SSH).

Who may call it

Requests from web pages with an http(s) origin are refused, so a page opened in the TV's browser cannot drive the service. Local apps and scripts (no Origin header) are accepted.

Endpoint Purpose GET /api/apps Installed apps, config, usage, version POST /api/launch {id, params} Launch an app GET /api/inputs HDMI inputs and their state POST /api/notify Picture notification (on the network: POST :8767/notify with the token) GET /api/voice/status, POST /api/voice/install, /uninstall, /set, /listen, /ask, /forget, /ha-test, /ha-agents Optional voice function and AI chat GET /api/theme/list, POST /api/theme/set, /revert Themes for the home screen; see Themes GET /api/live/status, /api/live/channels, /api/live/epg Live TV data POST /api/live/settings, /api/live/refresh, /api/live/reset Live TV setup GET /api/manager/status Versions, updates, options, hook state

items.title: Examples
items.text:
# launch an app
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/launch -d '{"id":"com.palm.app.settings"}'

# show a picture notification without a token (from the TV itself)
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/notify -d '{"title":"Hello","text":"From a shell","seconds":8}'

# the service version and updates
curl -s localhost:8765/api/manager/status

See the pages for Live TV, Picture notifications and Voice for their bodies.

items.title: Design
items.text: The home-screen design follows the Android TV project CleanYourTV (MIT). No code from it is used.

items.title: This documentation
items.text: Built with Zensical.

items.title: Debloat
items.text: An optional clean-up of LG's ads and telemetry. It is on by default in the setup and has a switch in the manager app.

items.title: What it does
items.text:
About a minute after every boot, the debloat:

  • stops the systemd services remotelogger, service-logger, contentminer and nudge;
  • prevents acr2, admanager, sportsalarm and adoverlay-service from starting, by mounting a do-nothing stub over each program (in RAM; the real files are not changed);
  • adds eic.ads.lgtvcommon.com, nl.ad.lgsmartad.com and nl.info.lgsmartad.com to /etc/hosts, pointing at 127.0.0.1 and ::1 and marked # cleanyourtv-debloat (other entries are untouched).

Nothing is uninstalled. It applies only while the launcher is Home, because LG's own Home needs some of those services to start; switching back to LG's Home lifts the debloat first.

items.title: Turning it off
items.text: Switch Debloat off in the manager app. It starts the stopped services again, unmounts the stubs and removes the marked hosts lines. To pause it without the manager, create /media/developer/cleanyourtv/DISABLE-DEBLOAT.

items.title: What it does not do
items.text: It does not block updates: firmware update blocking (for example with the Homebrew Channel's tools) is separate and is not touched. It does not claim to remove all tracking. It stops the services listed above and nothing else.

items.title: The Input key
items.text:
The remote's Input button opens an Inputs picker over the running app.

The picker shows the dock apps in a row, the inputs below (each with its port and what is connected, and a green dot on the active one) and, when Live TV is on, Live TV.

Key Action Left / Right Move Up / Down Switch rows OK Open Back or Input Close

The pointer works too.

items.title: What the key shows
items.text:
The Input button can show the Inputs list in three ways. Input key > Input key shows in the manager app chooses; each press of that row goes to the next one.

Choice What happens Default Over the running app, ready in the background A small app, com.cleanyourtv.picker, is started hidden after boot and the key only wakes it: instant. webOS 25 and newer Over the running app, started when pressed The same app is started by the key and closes itself after use (Back, a choice, or ten idle seconds). Nothing runs hidden, so it cannot keep the remote. The first moment takes longer. webOS before 10 The launcher's Inputs list The TV goes to Home with the Inputs list open. Needs CleanYourTV as Home; when LG's Home is selected the key stays with LG. none

On webOS 6.5 (reports) the hidden background app kept the remote and showed a loading circle, which is why older webOS starts it on demand. If the TV closes the background app three times in ten minutes, the service switches to started when pressed by itself (picker.mode: ondemand in config.json). Other overlay projects for rooted TVs also start their overlay on demand and close it after use.

items.title: How it works
items.text: It uses the bundled inputhook library, which injects a small hook into LG's input process so that a remote button can run a command. The Input button's code is 241 by default. The command opens the picker app (com.cleanyourtv.picker) over whatever is on screen.

items.title: Learning your remote's code
items.text:
Remotes differ. In the manager app, Input key > Learn the Input key reads the code of the button you press and tests that the picker opens. Clear restores the default.

The switch in the same menu removes the bind and gives the button back to LG's own picker. Learn the Home key is optional.

The Guide button can be bound the same way; that is part of Live TV (manager app > Live TV > Learn the Guide key).

When the hook is not attached

On some firmware the hook cannot attach. The manager then shows the Input key as not available and LG's picker is used.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
1. Root the TV and install the Homebrew Channel (rootmy.tv).
  2. From your computer, run the install command with the TV's IP address (below). It installs the CleanYourTV manager app.
  3. On the TV, open CleanYourTV and choose Set up now. It takes about a minute and the screen blinks once.

That is all. The launcher is LG's Home from then on.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• An LG webOS TV rooted with the Homebrew Channel.
  • SSH access to the TV as root, which the Homebrew Channel can enable (Settings > SSH Server).
  • Internet access on the TV (the install command downloads the package from GitHub).
  • webOS 5 or newer (2020 models and later). webOS 4 and older are not supported: they have no systemd and an old Node.js, and the setup stops before it changes anything.
  • Firmware from the tested TVs, or one where LG's Home app is of the flutter or web kind; see What happens on unlisted firmware.

Give the TV a fixed address

Reserve a fixed IP address for the TV in your router so the install command and the network notification address never change.

items.title: 1. Install the manager app
items.text:
From your computer, with your TV's IP address:

ssh root@192.168.1.50 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lasharor/cleanyourtv-WebOS/main/install.sh | sh'

The script downloads the latest release package, checks its SHA-256 and installs it. Nothing else on the TV changes in this step. The package can also be downloaded from Releases and installed with the Homebrew Channel or ares-install.

items.title: 2. Set up, on the TV
items.text:
Open CleanYourTV from the app list, choose the options and Set up now.

Option Default Debloat LG's ads and telemetry on Take over the Input key on

The setup:

  1. saves the original state in /media/developer/cleanyourtv/backup;
  2. installs the launcher and the service;
  3. adds boot scripts to /var/lib/webosbrew/init.d/;
  4. replaces LG's Home at boot (in RAM) and starts the service;
  5. checks that the new Home came up. If it did not, it removes the boot scripts and restarts the TV with LG's Home.

Its log is /media/developer/cytv-setup.log, kept across the restart, with the service log next to it in cytv-setup.log.service.

The same setup over SSH 

sh /media/developer/apps/usr/palm/services/com.cleanyourtv.manager.service/bootstrap.sh install
Options: --no-debloat, --no-input-key, --no-start, --no-verify, --force.

items.title: Unlisted firmware
items.text: The setup matches the TV's firmware against compat.json (it fetches the newest copy from the repository and falls back to the one in the package). A listed firmware is set up directly. For an unlisted firmware the setup continues when LG's Home app is the flutter or web kind, and otherwise stops and offers Set up anyway. To add a firmware to the list, open an issue with the output of Share log (Troubleshooting).

items.title: Installing a test build
items.text: To try a change that is not released yet, install from a branch: see Updating and uninstalling.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• The Home button opens LG's full-screen Home, not CleanYourTV. Some TVs have a Home Style setting. Set TV Settings > General > Home Settings > Home Style to Basic.
  • FAILED_IPKG_INSTALL. Remove the com.cleanyourtv.manager entry marked half-installed from /media/developer/apps/var/lib/opkg/status and install again.
  • Black screen after switching or rebooting. Wait a minute; if it stays black, restart the TV.

More in Troubleshooting.

items.title: The launcher
items.text: The launcher replaces LG's Home. It is a web page of the project that the TV's browser runs, so it starts fast and works the same on every supported webOS version.

items.title: The screen
items.text:
• Dock. Up to four apps, large, on the first row.
  • Top shelf. The name of the focused app and an ambient glow taken from its icon.
  • Grid. All other apps, sorted by how often you use each one (or A to Z).
  • Top buttons. Inputs, Live TV, Settings and Customise, and a clock. The buttons you see are yours to change.

items.title: Keys
items.text:
Action How Open an app OK App options (dock, hide) Hold OK on an app Remove a top button Hold OK on it Customise The Customise button Live TV The Live TV button or tile Switch input The Inputs button

The Magic Remote pointer works too: pointing and clicking, and holding the button on an app for its options.

items.title: Customise
items.text:
Customise holds:

  • the top buttons (add Inputs, Settings, Live TV or any app, or remove one),
  • hidden apps (show them again),
  • the app order (most used first, or A to Z),
  • the clock format (automatic, 12 or 24 hour),
  • Reset customisation.

The dock holds up to four apps. Hold OK on an app and choose Add to dock, Move left, Move right or Remove from dock.

items.title: Inputs
items.text: The Inputs button lists HDMI inputs by the names LG shows, with what is connected and a marker on the active one. OK switches to the input.

items.title: Icons
items.text:
Each tile uses the app's own icon. The tile colour is taken from the icon's edge colour, so an icon that reaches its edges blends into the tile, and the ambient glow comes from the icon's most vivid colour. Colours are worked out once per app and remembered.

Icons with a transparent margin

An icon that is an opaque square with a transparent margin around it (many LG icons) can look boxed in on its tile. A fix that fills the tile is available as a test build; see Test builds.

items.title: Language
items.text: Menus follow the TV's language: English, Dutch, German, French and Spanish.

items.title: Themes
items.text: The look of the home screen (colours, tile and text size, columns, clock, glow, animation speed, wallpaper) is a theme, chosen in the manager app.

items.title: Settings file
items.text:
Settings are stored on the TV in /media/developer/cleanyourtv/config.json:

Key Meaning dock App ids in the dock (up to four). topbar The buttons at the top. hidden App ids you hid. sort usage or alpha. clock auto, 12 or 24.

See config.example.json. Change settings in the launcher; the file is read and written by the service.

items.title: Live TV
items.text: Plays an IPTV playlist (M3U) from your own provider or server. It does not use LG's tuner, and the project provides no channels and no playlist.

items.title: Setting it up
items.text:
On first use the screen shows an address and a 6-digit code.

  1. Open the address on a phone or computer on the same network as the TV.
  2. Enter the code.
  3. Paste your M3U playlist address (and the XMLTV guide address if the playlist does not carry one).

The page closes by itself. It is open for ten minutes at most and only with the code.

From a shell on the TV instead:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/live/settings -d '{"playlistUrl":"http://...","epgUrl":"http://..."}'

items.title: Turning it off
items.text: Live TV is optional. In the manager app, Live TV > Show Live TV switches it on and off. Off hides it everywhere: the Live TV button and tile in the launcher, Live TV in the Inputs list, and the Guide key takeover (below). LG's own player and guide are used as before. The playlist and your favourites are kept, so switching it on again brings them back.

items.title: Keys
items.text:
Key Watching In the guide (OK) Up / Down, CH+ / CH- Next / previous channel Move; CH+ / CH- page Left / Right Channel banner (now and next) Previous / next tab Digits Jump to a channel number (playlist order) Same OK Open the guide Play the channel Guide Open the guide Close the guide Green Add / remove favourite Add / remove favourite Yellow Player menu (favourite, stream, statistics) Filters Blue Statistics Red Search (the TV's keyboard) Back Return to the launcher Clear filters and search, then close the guide

The tabs are All channels, Favourites, Recent and one per category of your playlist. Channels show badges for country, language and quality when the playlist names them (for example NL, EN, HD). Filters narrow the list by country, language and quality; search matches names across all channels.

items.title: The Guide button
items.text: By default the remote's Guide button belongs to LG. In the manager app, Live TV > Learn the Guide key records the button's code; afterwards it opens the Live TV channel guide over whatever is running, and closes it again when Live TV is open. Clear gives LG's guide back. The button is only taken over while Live TV is on and a code is learned. It uses the same hook as the Input key.

items.title: How it plays
items.text:
• The TV's own player plays HLS (.m3u8).
  • Stepping through channels with Up/Down starts the new channel only when the keys have paused for 180 ms. Channels you skip are never requested from your provider, which matters for accounts that allow one connection.
  • The player uses one video element for the whole session instead of creating one per channel.
  • The guide (XMLTV) is refreshed twice a day and keeps 36 hours.
  • When a playlist lists the same channel in several qualities (for example HD and SD), they are merged into one channel with several streams. If one does not start, the next is tried; a stream that stalls is reloaded once.
  • When a channel does not play, the screen says why: the server refused it, the stream is gone, it needs DRM, it is not video, or it is too slow.
  • Statistics (Blue) show the resolution, buffer, dropped frames and which stream is playing.

There is no recording and no pause.

items.title: Where it is stored
items.text:
The playlist address, which usually contains an access key, is stored only on the TV, in /media/developer/cleanyourtv/live/, readable by root only. To clear it:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/live/reset

Favourites, recent channels and the failed-channel list are stored in state.json in the same folder.

items.title: The manager app
items.text:
CleanYourTV in LG's app list sets up, updates and removes everything. The left side of the screen explains the focused row.

Row Function Launcher, Service Installed version; offers an update when the latest release is newer. Check for updates Asks GitHub for the latest release. Update channel Follow the stable releases or a test build. Go back to launcher Appears after a launcher update. CleanYourTV as Home Choose LG's Home or ours. The TV restarts. Theme Choose a theme (with its screenshot and description) from the list on GitHub; Theme options has the accent colour and going back. See Themes. Live TV Show Live TV (off hides it in the launcher and Inputs list and leaves the Guide button to LG), the Playlist (set up from your phone with a QR code and a 6-digit code), Refresh playlist and guide, Learn the Guide key, Clear recent channels and Remove the playlist. See Live TV. Input key The takeover switch, Learn the Input key, Input key shows (the Inputs list over the running app, ready in the background or started when pressed, or the launcher's own list) and the optional Learn the Home key. See The Input key. Voice Optional. Installs the speech recogniser (about 80 MB), learns the voice button, tries it, sets where the text goes. See Voice. Network notifications Switch, address, token and an example for sending picture notifications from other devices. Debloat Turns the debloat on or off. Share log A QR code that opens a masked diagnostic report on a phone, with a Copy button. Uninstall Removes everything and restarts the TV.

items.title: When the service is not running
items.text: The manager works without the service for two things: checking for a newer package and installing it, so a broken service can be repaired from the TV.

items.title: Share log
items.text:
Share log opens a short-lived page on your local network (port 8768 or higher, a random address, ten minutes). Scan the QR code with a phone on the same network. It works even when the service is not running, so it can also report a failed setup.

The report is masked: addresses, MAC addresses and URL paths are replaced, and the values of token, key, password, pass, secret and apikey are removed. It holds the TV model and firmware, the versions, LG's stock Home app, the mounts and boot scripts, whether our apps are registered, your options, the remote key codes seen by the input hook, the service status, the setup log, the last lines of the service log and the input hook log. Attach it to bug reports.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
Open CleanYourTV. The launcher (the home screen) and the service (the background part) update separately from the latest GitHub release, each checked against its SHA-256 file.

  • A launcher that does not start is replaced by the previous one, and a service that does not start by the previous files.
  • Go back to launcher returns to the previous launcher version after an update.
  • Before the setup, the app offers a newer package by itself.
  • Running the install command again also updates.

items.title: Update channel
items.text:
Update channel in the manager app chooses where updates come from.

Channel What it follows Stable releases The latest published release. This is the default. Test: branch A test build of a branch, made for people who are asked to try a change.

items.title: Test builds
items.text:
When a change needs to be tried on a TV the maintainer does not have, it is put on a branch. Every push to a branch other than main builds the package (.github/workflows/test-build.yml) and publishes it as a pre-release named test-<branch>. The stable updater never sees pre-releases.

Choose a test build Update channel lists the test builds (branch, commit, date). Pick one, then install it with the Launcher and Service rows. Back to the stable releases Update channel > Stable releases. The stable release is offered again, also when it is older than the test build. Install from scratch ssh root@<tv-ip> 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lasharor/cleanyourtv-WebOS/<branch>/install.sh \| CYTV_BRANCH=<branch> sh'. The manager then follows that branch. Same version number A test build records its commit in a BUILD file, so a newer push of the same version is still offered.

A test build can be less finished than a release

It is checked against its SHA-256 file like any release, but nobody has signed it. See Security.

items.title: Switching between LG's Home and the launcher
items.text:
Switching restarts the TV (about a minute).

Action How Use LG's Home CleanYourTV as Home off in the manager app. Use the launcher again CleanYourTV as Home on, from LG's app list. Over SSH touch /media/developer/cleanyourtv/DISABLE; reboot for LG's Home, rm /media/developer/cleanyourtv/DISABLE; reboot for ours. Failed boot The Homebrew Channel's failsafe mode skips all boot scripts; reboot again.

While LG's Home is selected the service still runs, so the manager app and the Input key keep working.

items.title: Uninstalling
items.text:
Uninstall in the manager app, or over SSH:

sh /media/developer/cleanyourtv/uninstall.sh

--keep-config keeps your settings and usage history, and --no-reboot restores LG's Home right away instead of restarting the TV. Uninstalling removes the apps, boot scripts and Input-key bind and restarts the TV, which then starts with LG's Home. See What it changes on the TV for what is removed.

items.title: Picture notifications
items.text: The com.cleanyourtv.notify app shows a card (picture, title, text) over whatever is on screen without taking the remote. Other devices send it with a POST request, for example Home Assistant showing a camera snapshot when the doorbell rings.

items.title: Enable it
items.text:
In the manager app: Network notifications > Accept notifications from the network. How to send then shows the address, the token and an example.

The token is a secret

Anyone who has it and can reach the TV can show cards on its screen. New token replaces it.

items.title: Sending one
items.text:
curl -X POST http://192.168.1.50:8767/notify \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Front door","text":"Someone is at the door","image":"http://192.168.1.20/snapshot.jpg","seconds":15,"position":"top-right"}'
Field Meaning title, text Up to 120 and 400 characters; either may be empty. image http(s) address of a picture, up to 6 MB. seconds Display time, 2 to 120 (default 8). position top, middle or bottom plus left, center or right (default top-right).

items.title: Home Assistant
items.text:
rest_command:
  tv_notify:
    url: "http://192.168.1.50:8767/notify"
    method: POST
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer <token>"
      Content-Type: "application/json"
    payload: '{"title":"{{ title }}","text":"{{ text }}","image":"{{ image }}","seconds":15}'

items.title: Limits and safety
items.text:
• The port (default 8767) and an allow list of addresses are in config.json under notifyApi: {"enabled":true,"port":8767,"allow":["192.168.1.0/24"]} (prefixes /8, /16 and /24 are supported).
  • Requests use plain HTTP, so the token is visible to anyone who can watch your network traffic. Keep the TV on a network you trust.
  • Ten wrong tokens lock an address out for ten minutes, and at most 20 notifications a minute are accepted.
  • From a shell on the TV, POST localhost:8765/api/notify accepts the same body without a token.

See Security.

items.title: What this changes on a TV
items.text:
CleanYourTV runs a service as root on a rooted TV. It listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 only. A few short-lived pages open on the local network on request, and an optional notification endpoint is off by default.

Port What When it is open 8765 (127.0.0.1 only) The service API Always; see Service API 8766 Live TV pairing page While you set up Live TV: a 6-digit code shown on the TV, ten minutes 8767 Network notifications Only when you switch it on in the manager app; needs a token 8768 and up Share-log page Ten minutes, at a random address, with a masked report 8769 Voice setup page Ten minutes, at a random 128-bit address, closed after saving

What the setup changes on the TV is listed in What it changes on the TV.

items.title: Network notifications
items.text: Off until switched on in the manager app. It then listens on port 8767 for POST /notify with Authorization: Bearer <token> (a random 192-bit token kept in config.json, readable by root only). It exposes only the notification call. Wrong tokens lock an address out for ten minutes, requests are limited to 20 a minute and 32 KB, and an optional allow list restricts addresses. It is plain HTTP: the token can be read by anyone who can watch the traffic on your network.

items.title: Themes
items.text: The manager downloads the theme list, screenshots, theme files and wallpapers from raw.githubusercontent.com (the main branch of this repository) over HTTPS, when you open Theme or choose a theme. They are data only: the service checks every value against its list, limits the sizes (theme 32 KB, wallpaper 1.5 MB, screenshot 600 KB), checks that images are images and refuses anything else. There is no script or CSS in a theme. Anything merged into main becomes available to every TV, which is the same trust you place in the releases of this repository; there is no signature.

items.title: Voice
items.text:
Optional and off by default. Installing it downloads files over HTTPS from PyPI, Ubuntu's archive and Moonshine's model server; each file is checked against a SHA-256 value written in the code, and a mismatch stops the install. The recogniser is a 64-bit program started by the root service with its own copy of the C library; it reads audio from a pipe and prints text.

  • Audio from the remote's microphone is held in memory only while recognising.
  • Only the recognised text is sent, and only to the address you set (plain http:// is possible: the token is then visible on your network) and, if you switch on AI chat, to openrouter.ai over HTTPS with your OpenRouter key and the model you chose. OpenRouter and that model's provider see the text.
  • The phone setup page is a short-lived page on the local network (port 8769, a random 128-bit address, ten minutes, closed after saving, plain HTTP: the key is visible on the network while it is typed).
  • With Home Assistant set up, the recognised text goes to the address you set, with your long-lived access token (plain http:// is possible: the token is then visible on your network; a self-signed certificate is accepted only when you switch that on).
  • The keys and the token are kept in config.json (readable by root only) and are never returned by the service.
  • Pausing LG's voice assistant sends it SIGSTOP; nothing of LG's is modified.

items.title: Trust
items.text: Everything it installs comes from this repository's GitHub releases and runs as root. Releases carry a SHA-256 file, which detects corruption but not a compromised repository. Download only from the release page of this repository.

items.title: Test builds
items.text: The manager's Update channel can follow a test build: a pre-release named test-<branch> that GitHub Actions publishes for each branch push. It is opt-in and off by default; the stable updater only reads the latest non-pre-release. A test build is downloaded over HTTPS from the repository the TV already updates from and checked against the .sha256 file in the same release, so the check protects against a damaged download, not against someone who can publish to the repository (the same is true of stable releases, which are not signed yet). The tag name is checked (test- and lower-case letters, digits and hyphens) and the files must be the package and launcher names the updater already expects.

items.title: Limits to know about
items.text:
• Any app on the TV can already run root commands through the Homebrew Channel; apps are not a security boundary on a rooted TV.
  • /media/developer is world-writable on webOS. The setup removes group and other write access from this project's files and keeps the playlist and settings files owner-only, but the parent folder remains writable.
  • The service API refuses requests from web pages (any http(s) origin); local apps and scripts are accepted.

Move from telnet to SSH

A rooted TV often has an unauthenticated telnet server open on the local network. Turn telnet off and SSH on in the Homebrew Channel's settings.

items.title: Reporting
items.text: Open a private security advisory on the GitHub repository, or an issue that does not include exploit details.

items.title: Tested TVs
items.text:
CleanYourTV is written for rooted LG webOS TVs. Only a few models have been tried, and reports are welcome: open an issue with the output of Share log (see Troubleshooting) and say whether it worked.

TV Firmware webOS (SDK) Status OLED65G26LA 33.23.05 webOS 25 (10.2.2) Tested. The maintainer's TV; everything in these pages was checked on it. Two models 23.25.55 Reported working. OLED65C54LA 43.21.77 SDK 11.2.0 Reported in issue #3: runs; app icons were drawn badly. A fix is available as a test build. 55UN7200PTF 04.64.00 webOS 5.6.2 (Node.js 8.12) Reported in issue #4: works with the Home Style set to Basic and a few fixes that are available as a test build.

What the status words mean

Tested means the maintainer ran it. Reported means someone else told us it works or what did not. A TV that is not on this list may still work: see unlisted firmware.

items.title: webOS version numbers
items.text:
LG names its webOS versions in two ways: a marketing name and the version the TV reports to software. The SDK version (Settings > About, or sdkVersion in the setup log) is the second one and is what the setup reads.

Marketing name First shipped on SDK version reported webOS 5 2020 5.x webOS 6 2021 6.x webOS 22 2022 7.x webOS 23 2023 8.x webOS 24 2024 9.x webOS 25 2025 10.x webOS 26 2026 11.x

LG also updates older TVs to newer versions, so the SDK version, not the model year, is what counts. The service avoids features the older versions lack: webOS 5 and 6 ship Node.js 8 (and Chromium 79 on webOS 6). The details are in Internals.

items.title: Themes
items.text:
A theme changes how the home screen looks: colours, the size of tiles and text, the number of columns, the clock, the ambient glow, the speed of animations and a wallpaper. Themes apply to the launcher's home screen (dock, top shelf, grid, top buttons and menus). Live TV, the Inputs picker and the notification cards keep their own look.

In the manager app, Theme lists the themes with a screenshot and a description of the highlighted one. Choosing one applies it; the home screen shows it the next time you open Home. Theme options holds the Accent colour (the colour of the focus ring and of the highlighted button or menu row, on top of any theme) and Go back to the previous theme.

items.title: Where the themes come from
items.text:
Themes are not part of the service. They are read from the themes/ folder of the GitHub repository (the main branch):

  • The manager downloads themes/index.json (the list) and the screenshots when you open Theme.
  • Choosing a theme downloads its theme.json and its wallpaper to the TV (/media/developer/cleanyourtv/themes/<id>/) and keeps them, so it keeps working offline. Choosing it again downloads the latest version. If GitHub cannot be reached, the list shows the themes that are already on the TV and says why.
  • Classic is built into the service and always works.
  • A theme is data only (values, an image): the service checks every value, limits the file sizes (theme 32 KB, wallpaper 1.5 MB, screenshot 600 KB) and checks that the images are images. There is no script or CSS in a theme.

items.title: The themes
items.text:
Theme What it is Classic The original look: near-black, white focus, ten columns. The default. Midnight Deep blue with a wallpaper and a blue focus. OLED black Pure black and no ambient glow, so unlit pixels stay off. Warm Brown and amber, with the glow in the accent colour and a wallpaper. Compact Twelve columns of smaller tiles: more apps on screen. Large print Eight columns of big tiles and larger text. Still No animation and a quiet glow. Bloom A flower wallpaper with the dock in a glass panel at the bottom. Down moves the dock up and the apps appear below it, centred.

The pictures are the launcher page rendered in a browser with each theme.

items.title: Contributing a theme
items.text:
Themes live in the repository, so a new one is a pull request:

  1. Copy a folder from themes/, for example classic, to themes/<id>/. The id is lower-case letters, digits and -.
  2. Edit theme.json; the rest keeps its default, or the value of the theme named in "extends".
  3. Add preview.jpg: a screenshot of the home screen with your theme (16:9, about 800 px wide, at most 600 KB). The TV shows it in the theme list.
  4. If it uses a wallpaper, add the image to the same folder (.jpg, .png or .webp, at most 1.5 MB, 1920 x 1080) and name it in effects.wallpaper. A wallpaper must be your own work or under a licence that allows redistribution; say which in the pull request.
  5. Run node tools/theme-index.js to update themes/index.json, then node tools/node8-check.js: it checks every theme folder against the schema, that the screenshot is there, and that the index is up to date.
  6. Open the pull request. Once it is merged into main, every TV can download the theme; no release is needed.

When you add a setting to the engine, add one row to SCHEMA in helper/theme.js, read its variable in app/index.html, and run node tools/theme-docs.js to regenerate the table below.

items.title: Making a theme with an AI assistant
items.text:
An assistant such as Claude can write a theme from a description ("a calm blue theme with big tiles and the dock at the bottom"). Give it a checkout of the repository (or these files) and the rules below.

What it needs to read - The table of settings further down this page (or SCHEMA in helper/theme.js, the source of that table): every key, its range and its default. - themes/classic/theme.json and one existing theme that is close to the goal, for example themes/bloom/theme.json. - themes/README.md for the folder layout.

Rules - A theme is data only: themes/<id>/theme.json with keys from the table, nothing else. No CSS, no script, no URLs. Unknown keys and out-of-range values are ignored or clamped, so a value that is not in the table has no effect. - Positions and sizes are pixels on a 1920 x 1080 canvas. Keep the clock and the buttons at least 60 px from the screen edges (TVs can crop the picture), and make sure the dock fits: dock.count x dock.w plus the gaps must be at most the screen width (a panel adds dock.panelPad on each side). - Text must stay readable: about 4.5 : 1 between colors.ink and the surfaces it sits on, and a visible focus ring. The text colour on the accent is chosen automatically. - The TV's graphics chip is weak: no blurred or animated wallpapers, one static image at most, 1920 x 1080, at most 1.5 MB (.jpg, .png or .webp), kept in the theme's folder and named in effects.wallpaper. Prefer the dock and grid settings over tricks. - A wallpaper must be original (drawn or generated for the theme) or under a licence that allows redistribution. Do not copy other people's artwork, screenshots or logos, and do not use brand names or trademarks in a theme. - Use "extends" to start from another theme and list only what changes. Do not rename a setting group: name, author, description and extends are the theme's own fields.

Steps 1. Create themes/<id>/theme.json (and the wallpaper, if any). 2. Look at it: node tools/theme-preview.mjs <id> --out /tmp/preview renders the home screen with made-up apps in headless Chrome and writes rest.png (home), grid.png (the focus moved down into the apps) and menu.png (a menu). It needs Node.js 22 or newer and Chrome. Open the images, fix what looks wrong (overlapping parts, unreadable text, clipped tiles) and render again. 3. When it looks right, node tools/theme-preview.mjs <id> --write also writes themes/<id>/preview.jpg (needs ffmpeg), the screenshot the TV shows. 4. node tools/theme-index.js updates themes/index.json; node tools/node8-check.js checks every theme folder, the screenshot and the index. 5. Commit and open a pull request; say where the wallpaper comes from.

A prompt to start with

Create a theme for CleanYourTV. Read the settings table in docs/themes.md, themes/classic/theme.json and themes/bloom/theme.json. The theme: describe the look and the layout you want. Write themes/<id>/theme.json using only keys from the table (data only; ranges are enforced), generate an original wallpaper if it needs one (1920 x 1080, under 1.5 MB, saved in the theme's folder), render it with node tools/theme-preview.mjs <id> --out /tmp/preview, look at rest.png, grid.png and menu.png, fix problems and render again, then run node tools/theme-preview.mjs <id> --write, node tools/theme-index.js and node tools/node8-check.js. Keep text readable and the wallpaper my own work.

items.title: Theme files
items.text:
A theme is themes/<id>/theme.json in the repository. Every key is optional. A missing or invalid value keeps the value of the theme named in "extends", or the default, which is the original look, so a theme lists only what it changes. Positions and sizes are in pixels on a 1920 x 1080 canvas.

{
  "name": "Midnight",
  "author": "CleanYourTV",
  "description": "Deep blue with a soft wallpaper and a blue focus.",
  "extends": "classic",
  "colors": { "night": "#060a18", "panel": "#101830", "ink": "#eaf0ff", "accent": "#7aa2ff" },
  "effects": { "glow": 0.8, "wallpaper": "midnight.jpg", "wallpaperDim": 0.25 }
}

items.title: What a theme can set
items.text:
Every part of the home screen has its own position and size, so themes can arrange the screen differently, not only recolour it: the clock, the top buttons (bar), the large app name, the dock and the grid. Each can be anchored to the top or bottom edge and aligned left, centre or right, with an offset. A dock at the bottom turns the grid into an overlay that opens when the focus moves down into it (Back or Up closes it); a dock at the top leaves the grid below it, scrolling.

A theme file holds values only. The service checks every value against the table and clamps numbers to their range; there is no CSS and no script, and a wallpaper is accepted only as a plain file name from the theme's folder that is also a real image of the right type. From a shell on the TV:

curl localhost:8765/api/theme/list
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/theme/set -d '{"id":"midnight","accent":"#ff8a3d"}'   # downloads the theme if it is not on the TV
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/theme/revert

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• Black screen after switching or rebooting. Wait a minute; if it stays black, restart the TV. If the new Home does not come up, the setup removes the boot scripts and restarts the TV with LG's Home by itself.
  • The Home button opens LG's full-screen Home, not CleanYourTV. Some TVs have a Home Style setting. Set TV Settings > General > Home Settings > Home Style to Basic.
  • An app is missing from the grid. Check Hidden apps in Customise. Apps without a launch icon are not listed.
  • After a firmware update removed root. Re-root, then run the install command and the setup again.
  • The Input key opens LG's picker. Check the Input key switch in the manager app and run Learn the Input key.
  • A loading circle appears every half minute and the remote stops responding until you hold Back. The Input key can show the Inputs list over the running app with a small app that the service starts in the background. On webOS 6.5 (reports) the TV closes that app again and it keeps the remote. From v1.5.13 webOS before 10 starts the app only when the key is pressed and closes it after use, and on any TV the service switches to that when it had to start the background app three times in ten minutes (picker.mode: ondemand in config.json). Input key > Input key shows chooses by hand; switching the Input key off entirely gives the key back to LG.
  • The manager list does not show Share log or Uninstall. Before v1.5.13 the list could not scroll; update, then move down: the list scrolls and fades where more rows are hidden.
  • Text appears twice in menus or the Live TV list on webOS 5 (blurred, overlapping). webOS 5's browser (Chromium 68) can keep the old text when a list is redrawn. From v1.5.13 the launcher swaps the list for a fresh element there instead of rewriting it.
  • The service restarts by itself. On some TVs Node.js 8 stops with uv_close: Assertion ... failed. From v1.5.13 the service logs its last operations when it finds that the previous run ended without a clean exit; they appear in Share log under the service log, so a report names the cause.
  • FAILED_IPKG_INSTALL. Remove the com.cleanyourtv.manager entry marked half-installed from /media/developer/apps/var/lib/opkg/status and install again.
  • Live TV shows the setup code again. The playlist address was reset or never saved; run the pairing again, or send it with POST /api/live/settings (Live TV).
  • Something is broken after an update. A launcher or service that does not start is replaced by the previous version automatically. Go back to launcher in the manager returns to the previous launcher by hand.
  • Back to LG's Home right now. In the manager, CleanYourTV as Home off, or sh /media/developer/cleanyourtv/undo-home.sh over SSH.

items.title: Reporting a problem
items.text:
An AI assistant can help you read the report and find the cause: see Working on problems with an AI assistant.

Open an issue and attach the output of Share log (manager app, see The manager app). It is masked, so it does not contain your addresses or keys. Say which TV and firmware you have and what you expected.

items.title: What it changes on the TV
items.text:
Only the takeover of Home and the debloat's /etc/hosts lines are applied in RAM at boot, as mounts. Everything else is stored in the writable partitions listed below and stays after a reboot until you uninstall. Nothing under /usr, /etc or the firmware is modified on disk, and a reboot without the boot scripts brings LG's Home back.

The optional voice download (about 80 MB) is stored in /media/developer/cleanyourtv/voice and stays until Remove voice or the uninstall. Optional features contact other services only when you switch them on; see Security.

items.title: At boot
items.text:
1. The Homebrew Channel runs the boot scripts in /var/lib/webosbrew/init.d/.
  2. 10-cleanyourtv-home starts the service and, unless /media/developer/cleanyourtv/DISABLE exists, bind-mounts a directory holding the launcher over LG's Home app (/usr/palm/applications/com.webos.app.home). The directory's appinfo.json is derived from this TV's own stock Home, so nothing of LG's is shipped.
  3. About a minute later the debloat runs, if it is on.

The bind mount lives in RAM. A reboot without the boot scripts, or the Homebrew Channel's failsafe mode, leaves LG's Home as it was.

items.title: Voice (optional)
items.text:
Recognises speech from the remote's microphone on the TV. The text is shown on screen and can be sent to a server you run, to a language model through OpenRouter, or both; the answer is shown as text on screen. Answers are not spoken. No audio is recorded or sent anywhere.

It is off and not installed by default. Nothing described here runs until you install it.

items.title: Installing
items.text:
Voice in the manager app downloads about 80 MB into /media/developer/cleanyourtv/voice. The checksums are pinned in the code; Remove voice deletes everything again.

Part From Speech engine libmoonshine.so and ONNX Runtime the moonshine-voice 0.1.5 package on PyPI (MIT) 64-bit C library ubuntu-base 22.04.5 for arm64 (this TV has a 32-bit userland on a 64-bit kernel, so the 64-bit recogniser brings its own) Model tiny-streaming-en (34 million parameters, int8) download.moonshine.ai (MIT) cytv-asr, a small program that feeds audio to the engine this repository (voice/asr.c, built with voice/build.sh)

items.title: Using it
items.text:
Step How Choose the button Voice > Learn the voice button. Try the remote's microphone button; if the hook does not see it, any spare button works. Then switch Listen on the voice button on. Try without a button Voice > Try it now, or curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/listen Send the text to a server curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"url":"http://server:port/path","token":"optional"}' Pause LG's voice assistant Voice > Switch off LG's voice assistant. It pauses LG's voiceconductor process while voice is on, so LG's own screen and its cloud recognition do not start on the same button. A reboot or turning the switch off undoes it.

On screen a card changes in place while you speak: Listening (moving bars), Recognising or Thinking (dots), then your question in small type above the answer. Reading time follows the length of the answer.

items.title: Sending text to your own server
items.text: The TV sends POST with the JSON body {"text":"...","source":"cleanyourtv","language":"en","time":"..."} and, when a token is set, Authorization: Bearer <token>. If the server answers with JSON ({"title","text","image","seconds"}) or plain text, the answer is shown as a card. The address and token are stored in config.json on the TV only.

items.title: AI chat (OpenRouter)
items.text:
In Voice, Set up from your phone shows a QR code. Scan it with a phone on the same Wi-Fi and enter:

  • your OpenRouter key,
  • a model (the list is read from OpenRouter; any model name can be typed),
  • instructions, and, if you like, the address of your own server.

The page is open for ten minutes or until you save, at a random address. It is plain HTTP, so use it on a network you trust. Model on the TV chooses among the newest models of the main providers, with their price. AI chat (OpenRouter) switches the answers on and off.

The same from a shell:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"llm":{"key":"sk-or-...","model":"openrouter/auto"}}'
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"llm":{"enabled":true}}'

What you say is sent as text to openrouter.ai with the model you chose (a short instruction asks for one to three plain sentences; change it with "system"), and the answer appears on screen. The model remembers the last six exchanges for ten minutes (Forget the conversation clears them). The key is stored in config.json on the TV only. With a server address set as well, the server also receives the text and the model's answer ({"text","answer"}).

You can also ask by text, with the same result, and without the speech download:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/ask -d '{"text":"..."}'

It answers {"text","answer","error"}; add "card":false to skip the screen.

items.title: The speech model
items.text:
Moonshine (Moonshine AI, MIT licence) runs on the TV; there is no cloud recogniser.

Model tiny-streaming-en: about 34 million parameters, encoder and decoder, int8 weights, 45 MB. Runtime ONNX Runtime on the CPU (two ARM cores on the G2). Segmentation The engine's voice-activity detection splits the audio into phrases. The service stops recording after 1.2 s of silence, after 7 s without speech, or after 15 s. Cost on the G2 Load 0.3 s; a 3 s phrase takes about 1.4 s; about 190 MB of memory while recognising, none when idle. Reported accuracy 12.0 % average word error rate on the Open ASR Leaderboard datasets, 4.8 % on LibriSpeech test-clean (figures from the Moonshine project; not measured through the remote's microphone). Language English. Moonshine also publishes German, Spanish, Arabic, Japanese, Mandarin, Tagalog and Vietnamese models and larger English ones (small 123 M, medium 245 M parameters). Audio 16 kHz mono from the microphone stream of LG's voiceinput service. Held in memory while recognising, then discarded; not written to disk or sent anywhere.

The TV's programs are 32-bit ARM on a 64-bit kernel and the recogniser is a 64-bit program, so cytv-asr runs through the 64-bit loader and libraries that the download places in the same folder. Nothing in the system folders is changed.

Only text goes further: to your server, to OpenRouter, or nowhere. LG's own assistant is a separate path with its own cloud recognition; Switch off LG's voice assistant pauses it while voice is on.

items.title: Home Assistant (Assist)
items.text:
The recognised text can go to Home Assistant's Assist (POST /api/conversation/process), which turns on lights, answers questions about your home and so on. Its answer is shown as text on the card. Answers are not spoken.

In Voice, Set up from your phone also asks for:

  • the address of Home Assistant, for example http://homeassistant.local:8123,
  • a long-lived access token (your Home Assistant profile page, under Security),
  • whether to accept a self-signed certificate (only matters for https:// addresses),
  • which answers first.

Choosing Home Assistant (Assist) in the menu tests the connection and shows the name and version of your Home Assistant.

Setting Behaviour Home Assistant first, then the AI (default) The text goes to Assist. If Assist understood it, its answer is shown. If it did not (no_intent_match), or Home Assistant cannot be reached, the same text goes to the AI chat, when that is switched on. Without the AI, Assist's own message is shown. Home Assistant only The AI is never asked. The AI only Home Assistant is not asked.

Assist agent lists the conversation agents of your Home Assistant (its conversation.* entities) and lets you choose one; the default is the built-in agent. A conversation id is passed on, so follow-up questions keep their context; a new conversation starts after ten quiet minutes or after Forget the conversation.

The same from a shell:

curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"ha":{"url":"http://homeassistant.local:8123","token":"eyJ..."}}'
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/set -d '{"ha":{"route":"ha-only","agent":"conversation.home_assistant","selfSigned":false}}'
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/ha-test
curl -X POST localhost:8765/api/voice/ask -d '{"text":"turn on the living room light"}'

route is ha-first, ha-only or ai-only; {"ha":{"clear":true}} removes the address and the token. /api/voice/ask answers {"text","answer","via","error"}, where via is ha or ai.

The token is stored in config.json on the TV only and is never returned by the service. Only the recognised text goes to your Home Assistant. With a plain http:// address the token is visible on your network.

items.title: Contributing
items.text: The code is on GitHub. Issues and pull requests are welcome, especially reports from TVs that are not in the tested list.

items.title: Layout
items.text: Folder or file What it is app/ The launcher: one HTML file of plain JavaScript, with version.json. manager/, picker/, notify/ The three apps of the package (manager, Inputs picker, picture notification card). themes/ The themes: one folder each (theme.json, preview.jpg, a wallpaper) and index.json. Read by the TVs from GitHub, not shipped with the service; contribute one. helper/ The root service (Node.js): API, Live TV, notifications, voice, manager, input hook, share log, self-update. scripts/ Boot, setup and restore scripts: bootstrap.sh, 10-cleanyourtv-home, stage-home.sh, undo-home.sh, the debloat scripts. shared/ flexgap.js, added to every page by the build for older Chromium. voice/ Source of the small speech program cytv-asr and its build script. third-party/ The bundled inputhook files and the QR library. tools/ node8-check.sh: service and theme checks under Node 8.12.0; theme-docs.js: regenerates the table of theme settings in the docs; theme-index.js: writes themes/index.json; theme-preview.mjs: renders a theme in headless Chrome (and makes its screenshot). ipk/build.py Builds the release files. compat.json The list of tested firmware the setup reads. install.sh, uninstall.sh The installer and uninstaller. docs/, zensical.toml This documentation.

items.title: Building
items.text:
python3 ipk/build.py

writes the release files to dist/: com.cleanyourtv.manager_<version>_all.ipk, frontend-<version>.tgz and a .sha256 file for each. Attach them to a GitHub release tagged v<version>. The service version is VERSION in helper/helper.js; the launcher version is app/version.json and VERSION in app/index.html (the build refuses to run when they differ).

Using an AI assistant to find or fix a bug is welcome: see Working on problems with an AI assistant and AGENTS.md in the repository root.

items.title: Rules of the road
items.text:
• Support webOS 5. The service must run on Node.js 8: no crypto.randomInt, no fs.promises, no URL as a global, no mkdirSync({recursive}), no http.get(url, options). Use helper/netcompat.js. tools/node8-check.sh catches regressions.
  • The pages run in Chromium 79 and newer. The launcher is written in plain ES5 style without a framework, and only transform and opacity are animated, because the TV's GPU is weak. No flex gap without the polyfill the build adds.
  • Do not store private data in the repository. No playlist addresses, access keys, IP addresses or names.
  • Documentation must match the code. When a feature changes, change its page here and, if it is mentioned there, the README.
  • Licence. The project is MIT. Do not copy code from GPL projects into it; describe behaviour and write your own.

items.title: Adding a TV to the tested list
items.text: Open an issue with the output of Share log and say whether it worked. A pull request that adds an entry to compat.json is welcome too: firmware, optionally sdk, homeType, status and a note.

items.title: Test builds
items.text: Push a branch and the workflow publishes a test build that people can install from the manager app. See Testing and CI.

items.title: The pieces
items.text: Piece Runs as Notes The service (helper.js and modules) Node.js, root, started by the boot script Listens on 127.0.0.1:8765; bridges the web pages to luna-send (LG's service bus), serves app icons, runs Live TV, notifications, voice, the manager API and the input hook. The launcher (app/index.html) A web app in LG's web runtime, mounted as LG's Home Reads apps and settings from the service. Manager, picker, notify Web apps installed from the package The picker and notify apps are hidden; the service starts them. The input hook Injected into LG's input processes Runs a command when a bound remote key is pressed.

items.title: How the launcher becomes Home
items.text:
1. 10-cleanyourtv-home runs at boot and starts the service.
  2. stage-home.sh builds a directory holding the launcher plus an appinfo.json derived from this TV's own stock Home (saved in backup/home-appinfo.orig.json the first time), switched to the web type.
  3. The script bind-mounts that directory over /usr/palm/applications/com.webos.app.home, restarts the system app manager (sam) so it reads the new Home, and launches Home again.
  4. A watchdog keeps checking that the service answers. If it stays unreachable for about a minute, it restores LG's Home until the next reboot.

Nothing is written under /usr: the mount disappears at reboot. DISABLE in /media/developer/cleanyourtv makes the script skip it.

items.title: Updates and rollback
items.text:
• Launcher. The manager downloads frontend-<version>.tgz and its .sha256, checks the list of files in the archive (only app/...), unpacks, checks version.json, swaps it in (the old one becomes app.prev), reloads Home and waits up to 40 seconds for the new launcher to report that it started. If it does not, the previous launcher is swapped back.
  • Service. The manager downloads the package, installs it with the system's app installer and runs bootstrap.sh update, which keeps the running files in backup/service-prev.tgz, copies the new ones, restarts the service and waits for it to answer with the new version. If it does not, the previous files are restored.
  • Test builds. Same flows, from a pre-release; the commit in a BUILD file is how two builds with one version number are told apart.

items.title: Older webOS versions
items.text:
webOS 5 and 6 ship Node.js 8, and webOS 6 has Chromium 79.

  • helper/netcompat.js supplies URL, URLSearchParams, crypto.randomInt, mkdir -p and the http(s).get(url, options) form.
  • shared/flexgap.js is added to every page by the build; where flex gap is ignored it applies the spacing as margins.
  • The service accepts the file://<appId>-webos origin that webOS 6 apps send, for our own apps and the Home slot only.
  • scripts/reload-home.sh restarts webapp-mgr on webOS 6, where a relaunch alone keeps the old page.

Not yet tried on a webOS 5 or 6 TV

These changes follow a community fork for webOS 6 and a report from a webOS 5.6.2 TV. The service is tested under Node 8.12.0 (tools/node8-check.sh) and the pages in a current Chrome with the detection switched off, but not on a TV of those versions.

items.title: Things that were tried
items.text:
A native launcher

A launcher written in C with SDL2 (so it draws on the GPU without the web runtime) was built and run as LG's Home on a webOS 25 TV. It worked, started quickly and used about as much memory and CPU as the web launcher, but LG's compositor shows "Do you want to exit the app?" when Back is pressed in a native app, and setting a key mask on the window did not stop it. It is kept on the native-launcher branch for reference and is not part of the project.

items.title: Service checks under Node 8
items.text:
webOS 5 TVs ship Node.js 8.12. tools/node8-check.sh downloads that exact version (from nodejs.org, checksum verified, cached in ~/.cache/cleanyourtv) and runs tools/node8-check.js with it:

sh tools/node8-check.sh

The checks:

  • parse every service file;
  • load every module;
  • run the compatibility layer against a local server (http requests, mkdir -p, URL, randomInt);
  • run the Live TV pairing end to end: the code, a wrong code, saving the playlist, fetching and parsing it;
  • run the update logic of the manager against a mock of the GitHub API: the stable and test channels, equal versions with different commits, and going back to stable.

Nothing leaves your machine. The script also runs on current Node: node tools/node8-check.js.

items.title: Pages
items.text:
The pages are plain HTML with no build step, so they can be opened in a desktop Chrome with a small mock of the service on 127.0.0.1:8765 and driven with scripted key events. That is how the launcher, Live TV and manager screens are checked before they go to a TV. The mock needs to answer /api/apps, /api/live/* and /api/manager/* with the shapes in Service API.

What cannot be checked on a computer

Playback of real streams, the TV's remote and pointer, the on-screen keyboard and anything that depends on LG's compositor need a TV.
